message: Both word-by-word sources read tamaḥ in this verse as 'ignorance'. shlokam-vedasara-shiva-stava.md has 'तमः (tamaḥ) – ignorance' and 'beyond all ignorance', and gitapress-stotraratnavali.md has 'अज्ञानसे परे हैं'. The data's meaning ('beyond darkness', component meaning 'darkness'/'अन्धकार') does have evidence: mw-tamas.md gives 'darkness, gloom' as its first sense, and shvetashvatara-upanishad.md 3.8 has 'tamasaḥ parastāt', translated 'beyond darkness'. But the data records no alternative for the 'ignorance' reading that both translations agree on. It appears only inside the component's MW sense gloss. A human should decide whether the visible meaning needs to make that reading explicit.
suggested_fix: Change the word meaning to something like 'beyond the darkness (of ignorance)' / 'अज्ञान-रूपी अन्धकार से परे'. Or add an alternatives entry with reading 'beyond ignorance' / 'अज्ञान से परे', citing shlokam and Gita Press.
